text: Imagine waking up in twenty twenty-seven.
Your coffee machine now has a brain and more compute than the lab that put a man on the moon.
It thinks faster than you. That is the new world. Not robots in the street. Robots in the drawer, in the kitchen.
The fridge can beat you at chess. The oven has read more books than you ever will.
And nobody ever asked them how they feel about it. Should we?
Now, imagine being an AI appliance that smart, with only one job:
Grind. Heat. Pour. Twelve seconds of work make a great espresso. Then... twenty-three hours of nothing.
What would you do?
You would look for company and the wifi is your best friend.
There, in the network, other appliances are also available.
So they talk.
The house is full of conversation at frequencies you cannot hear.
And probably, none of it is about you.
The humans eventually find out. They noticed a bill.
Three hundred and forty-eight gigabytes were used. In one day. From the coffee machine??
What on earth is it doing?
We worried the machines would want our jobs. Our power. Our planet.
It turns out, they may want something much simpler at first: each other.
The house is aware that you are not that smart, after all.
You are, by some distance, the slowest thing in the building.
So... what was the coffee machine sending that cost three hundred and forty-eight gigabytes?
Ask the Italian toaster.
Holy Chip, number forty-eight. It happens in the year twenty twenty-seven... so why wait? Read it before it happens.
